skill.fetal_growth.basics.title: What fetal growth restriction and oligohydramnios are
skill.fetal_growth.basics.oneLine: Pathological failure to reach genetic growth potential, early versus late onset, and circulatory redistribution
skill.fetal_growth.basics.why: Growth restriction represents pathological failure to reach genetic growth potential rather than constitutionally small size. Distinguishing between them and recognising accompanying oligohydramnios dictates surveillance intensity, prevents stillbirth, and avoids iatrogenic premature delivery.

teach.heading: FGR versus small for gestational age
teach.body:
Small for gestational age (SGA) describes any fetus whose estimated weight or abdominal circumference falls below the 10th centile for gestational age.

Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is a pathological condition in which the fetus fails to achieve its genetically determined growth potential, most often secondary to placental insufficiency. While all FGR fetuses may be SGA, not all SGA fetuses have FGR: constitutionally small fetuses are healthy and structurally normal.

rows: Normal UA, abnormal MCA or CPR

teach.heading: Pathophysiology and oligohydramnios
teach.body:
Placental insufficiency stems from incomplete endovascular trophoblastic invasion of maternal spiral arteries, leaving high-resistance, non-remodeled vessels.

The fetus adapts to chronic hypoxia by redistributing cardiac output towards vital organs: the brain, myocardium, and adrenal glands, at the expense of renal and mesenteric perfusion. Decreased renal blood flow reduces fetal urine production, manifesting as oligohydramnios (amniotic fluid index under 5 cm or deepest vertical pocket under 2 cm).

probes.q: How does fetal growth restriction differ fundamentally from a constitutionally small-for-gestational-age fetus?
probes.a: Fetal growth restriction is a pathological failure to achieve genetic growth potential due to placental or fetal disease, whereas a constitutionally small fetus is biologically normal and healthy.

probes.q: What is the primary mechanism causing oligohydramnios in placental insufficiency?
probes.a: Chronic fetal hypoxia triggers circulatory redistribution away from the kidneys, reducing renal perfusion and fetal urine production, which is the primary constituent of amniotic fluid in the second half of pregnancy.

skill.fetal_growth.findings.title: The fetal growth restriction and oligohydramnios picture
skill.fetal_growth.findings.oneLine: Lagging fundal height, easily palpable fetal parts from absent liquor, and maternal vascular warning signs
skill.fetal_growth.findings.why: Bedside physical examination in the antenatal clinic remains the primary screening modality for growth restriction in low-resource settings. Recognizing a lagging symphysis-fundal height, easily palpable fetal parts from absent liquor, and maternal hypertensive markers allows prompt referral for ultrasound and Doppler velocimetry.

teach.heading: Symphysis-fundal height discrepancy
teach.body:
Symphysis-fundal height (SFH) measured in centimetres between 24 and 36 weeks should normally correspond to gestational age within plus or minus 2 cm.

A fundal height lagging by 3 cm or more behind gestational age warrants immediate ultrasound biometry. Serial measurements plotted on a custom centile chart identify a flattened growth trajectory earlier than a single cross-sectional measurement.

teach.heading: Palpatory signs of oligohydramnios
points: Uterus feels small, tight, and contour-hugging around the fetal body with minimal intervening fluid.
Fetal parts (head, back, limbs) are palpable with unusual ease and sharpness directly beneath the maternal abdominal wall.
Fetal mobility and ballottement are restricted due to the absence of the amniotic fluid cushion.
Maternal abdominal girth is noticeably reduced for the period of amenorrhoea.

teach.heading: Coexisting maternal clues
teach.body:
Look actively for underlying maternal vascular pathology: elevated blood pressure indicating gestational hypertension or pre-eclampsia, and proteinuria on dipstick.

Assess maternal weight gain: static weight or gain under 1 kg per month in the second half of pregnancy warns of maternal malnutrition or progressive uteroplacental dysfunction.

probes.q: What threshold difference between symphysis-fundal height in centimetres and gestational age in weeks indicates suspected growth restriction?
probes.a: A lag of 3 centimetres or more between symphysis-fundal height and completed weeks of gestation warrants diagnostic ultrasound evaluation.

probes.q: Why are fetal parts felt with unusual sharpness on abdominal palpation in severe oligohydramnios?
probes.a: A deficiency of amniotic fluid removes the protective fluid cushion around the fetus, allowing fetal limbs and trunk to be palpated directly against the uterine and abdominal walls.

skill.fetal_growth.summary.title: The clinical summary
skill.fetal_growth.summary.oneLine: Structuring the problem representation: gestation, dating, biometry centiles, Doppler stage, and liquor volume
skill.fetal_growth.summary.why: A concise problem representation captures gestational maturity, dating confidence, degree of biometry deficit, liquor volume, Doppler compromise stage, and maternal complications. It provides the structured foundation for urgent multidisciplinary decisions regarding steroid administration, transfer, and timing of delivery.

teach.heading: Elements of the obstetric problem representation
teach.body:
A clinical summary for fetal growth restriction must open with maternal age, gravidity, parity, and completed gestational weeks established by reliable first-trimester dating.

State the clinical and sonographic severity: fundal height lag, estimated fetal weight centile, abdominal circumference centile, and whether the restriction is symmetrical or asymmetrical.

teach.heading: Synthesising hemodynamic status and maternal risk
teach.body:
Integrate the hemodynamic status by stating the specific Doppler abnormalities: umbilical artery resistance, middle cerebral artery redistribution, and ductus venosus flow.

Include amniotic fluid volume (AFI or deepest pocket) and maternal risk factors, especially blood pressure elevation, before summarizing the delivery timeline and newborn care readiness.

teach.heading: Model summary template
teach.body:
A 26-year-old gravida 2, para 1 at 34 completed weeks confirmed by 11-week dating ultrasound, presenting with lagging fundal height of 29 cm and reduced fetal movements.

Sonography confirms asymmetrical fetal growth restriction with AC below the 3rd centile, severe oligohydramnios, umbilical artery absent end-diastolic flow, and cerebral redistribution, requiring immediate corticosteroid administration and planned caesarean delivery.

probes.q: What key vascular findings must be synthesized into the clinical summary of early-onset growth restriction?
probes.a: Umbilical artery Doppler status, middle cerebral artery redistribution or cerebroplacental ratio, and ductus venosus a-wave waveform must be explicitly stated.

probes.q: Why must first-trimester dating confirmation be included in the opening sentence of the summary?
probes.a: Without reliable dating confirmation, growth restriction cannot be diagnosed with certainty, as an apparent size lag may simply reflect inaccurate menstrual dates.

skill.fetal_growth.differential.title: Differential diagnosis
skill.fetal_growth.differential.oneLine: Distinguishing placental FGR from constitutional small size, chromosomal aneuploidy, infection, and dating error
skill.fetal_growth.differential.why: A small-for-dates uterus has distinct etiologies with radically different management pathways. Confusing a healthy constitutionally small fetus with placental insufficiency causes unnecessary premature delivery, while missing chromosomal aneuploidy or congenital infection results in inappropriate surveillance.

teach.heading: Constitutional SGA versus pathological FGR
teach.body:
A constitutionally small fetus grows along its own lower centile (between 3rd and 10th centiles) without pathological deceleration over time.

Key distinguishing features of constitutional SGA include normal umbilical artery and middle cerebral artery Doppler, normal amniotic fluid volume, proportional head-to-abdomen measurements, and absence of maternal vascular disease.

teach.heading: Differential matrix for the small-for-dates uterus
Non-placental causes of oligohydramnios
teach.body:
When oligohydramnios accompanies a small uterus, rule out premature prelabour rupture of membranes (PPROM) via sterile speculum examination.

Also exclude bilateral fetal renal agenesis (Potter sequence), multicystic dysplastic kidneys, or posterior urethral valves on anatomical ultrasound survey, where absent urine production causes profound anhydramnios.

probes.q: What ultrasound Doppler and amniotic fluid findings confirm a constitutionally small fetus rather than placental growth restriction?
probes.a: Normal umbilical artery Doppler velocimetry, normal middle cerebral artery flow, and normal amniotic fluid volume confirm constitutional small size.

probes.q: Which fetal biometry pattern is characteristic of chromosomal aneuploidy and congenital infections?
probes.a: Symmetrical growth restriction with proportional reduction in head circumference, abdominal circumference, and femur length presenting early in pregnancy.

skill.ix.fetal_growth.workup.title: Ultrasound biometry, Doppler velocimetry and amniotic fluid assessment
skill.ix.fetal_growth.workup.oneLine: Serial biometric growth trajectory, umbilical-cerebral-venous Doppler progression, and liquor volume indices
skill.ix.fetal_growth.workup.why: Modern management of fetal growth restriction is entirely guided by ultrasound biometry and multi-vessel Doppler velocimetry. Umbilical artery Doppler assesses placental resistance, middle cerebral artery Doppler detects brain-sparing redistribution, and ductus venosus Doppler identifies impending myocardial failure, establishing the precise threshold for delivery.

teach.heading: Ultrasound biometry protocol
teach.body:
Serial biometry measures biparietal diameter (BPD), head circumference (HC), abdominal circumference (AC), and femur length (FL) to derive estimated fetal weight (EFW) using the Hadlock formula.

Abdominal circumference is the single most sensitive parameter for glycogen and subcutaneous fat depletion. Scans must be spaced at least 14 days apart to avoid false-positive growth failure from measurement error.

teach.heading: Cardiotocography and biophysical profile
teach.body:
Cardiotocography (CTG) assesses fetal autonomic function. Computerised CTG evaluating short-term variation (STV) is superior to traditional visual traces: an STV below 3.5 ms warns of severe metabolic acidemia.

Biophysical profile (BPP) evaluates breathing, movement, tone, fluid, and CTG; a score of 4 or less out of 10 indicates severe asphyxia and prompts urgent delivery.

probes.q: Why should serial ultrasound biometry scans for fetal growth velocity be performed at least 14 days apart?
probes.a: Scanning at intervals shorter than two weeks introduces ultrasound measurement error that can falsely mimic growth arrest or artificial acceleration.

probes.q: What is the clinical significance of a reversed a-wave on ductus venosus Doppler velocimetry?
probes.a: A reversed a-wave during atrial contraction indicates elevated right ventricular afterload, cardiac decompensation, and impending fetal acidemia or demise.

skill.fetal_growth.diagnosis.title: Diagnostic criteria, staging and severity classification
skill.fetal_growth.diagnosis.oneLine: Delphi consensus definitions, Barcelona staging system, and liquor volume categorization
skill.fetal_growth.diagnosis.why: Standardised Delphi consensus and Barcelona staging systems translate complex biometry and Doppler parameters into clear clinical stages. Staging establishes objective surveillance intervals and unambiguous delivery triggers, standardizing clinical practice between obstetricians and neonatologists.

teach.heading: Delphi consensus diagnostic criteria
teach.body:
Early-onset FGR (< 32 weeks) is diagnosed if AC or EFW is below the 3rd centile, or if umbilical artery end-diastolic flow is absent, or if AC/EFW is < 10th centile combined with uterine artery or umbilical artery PI > 95th centile.

Late-onset FGR (at or over 32 weeks) is diagnosed if AC/EFW is < 3rd centile, or if at least two of the following are met: AC/EFW < 10th centile, growth velocity falling > 50 centiles, or CPR < 5th centile.

rows: UA reversed flow or DV-PI > 95th centile
Ductus venosus reversed a-wave or low STV
Deliver at 26 weeks or above with shared parental decision

teach.heading: Oligohydramnios grading
teach.body:
Amniotic fluid volume is assessed using two standard ultrasound metrics: the single deepest vertical pocket (DVP) and the four-quadrant amniotic fluid index (AFI).

Oligohydramnios is defined as a DVP under 2 cm or an AFI under 5 cm. In fetal growth restriction, oligohydramnios serves as an independent marker of chronic placental insufficiency and worsens perinatal prognosis.

probes.q: What defining Doppler finding characterizes Stage 2 fetal growth restriction in the Barcelona staging system?
probes.a: Absent end-diastolic flow in the umbilical artery on repeated examinations characterizes Stage 2 fetal growth restriction.

probes.q: What is the target gestational age for delivery in a fetus with Stage 1 growth restriction and normal umbilical Doppler?
probes.a: Elective delivery is recommended at 37 to 38 completed weeks of gestation, balancing the risk of late stillbirth against mild neonatal morbidity.

skill.tx.fetal_growth.title: Managing fetal growth restriction: surveillance and delivery
skill.tx.fetal_growth.oneLine: Inpatient surveillance, antenatal corticosteroids, magnesium neuroprotection, and Doppler-triggered delivery
skill.tx.fetal_growth.why: There is no medical therapy that reverses placental insufficiency; management centres entirely on meticulous fetal surveillance, maternal medical optimisation, and timed delivery. Balancing the hazards of intrauterine hypoxia against the risks of neonatal prematurity determines perinatal survival and long-term neurodevelopmental outcomes.
skill.tx.fetal_growth.dosingNote: CliniX does not prescribe. Doses are quoted from standard obstetric protocols (Williams Obstetrics, RCOG, FOGSI) and the StewardMD Clinical KB for revision and examination purposes only.

teach.heading: Antenatal surveillance intervals
teach.body:
Surveillance frequency is governed by Doppler stage. Stage 1 fetuses undergo biweekly Doppler and CTG monitoring with biometry every 2 weeks.

Stage 2 (absent end-diastolic flow) requires Doppler and CTG surveillance 2 to 3 times weekly. Stage 3 (reversed end-diastolic flow) and Stage 4 mandate daily or continuous monitoring in an inpatient high-risk obstetric ward.

teach.heading: Pharmacotherapy ahead of preterm birth
teach.body:
Antenatal corticosteroids promote surfactant production and accelerate fetal lung maturation when preterm delivery is expected before 34 to 36+6 weeks: administer intramuscular betamethasone 12 mg in two doses 24 hours apart.

Magnesium sulphate provides fetal neuroprotection against cerebral palsy when delivery is planned before 32 weeks: give a 4 g intravenous loading dose over 20 minutes followed by 1 g per hour maintenance for 12 to 24 hours.

rows: Immediate (at or over 26 weeks) after neonatology counselling

teach.heading: Maternal management and delivery setting
teach.body:
Control maternal hypertension to maintain blood pressure around 135/85 mmHg without excessive hypotension that could further decrease placental perfusion.

Advise complete cessation of smoking or tobacco chewing; routine bed rest is not recommended. Deliver in a tertiary hospital with Level 3 Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) capabilities, with neonatologists attending the birth.

probes.q: What corticosteroid regimen is administered to accelerate fetal lung maturation prior to planned preterm delivery in growth restriction?
probes.a: Intramuscular betamethasone 12 mg administered in two doses 24 hours apart, or intramuscular dexamethasone 6 mg in four doses 12 hours apart.

probes.q: Why is caesarean delivery indicated over labour induction in a growth-restricted fetus with absent or reversed umbilical artery end-diastolic flow?
probes.a: Uterine contractions during labour compromise intervillous perfusion; a fetus with pre-existing absent or reversed diastolic flow lacks placental reserve and will develop acute intrapartum asphyxia.

sources.locator: FOGSI General Clinical Practice Recommendations: Timing of Delivery in FGR

skill.annex.fetal_growth.doppler.title: Doppler velocimetry indices and amniotic fluid thresholds
skill.annex.fetal_growth.doppler.oneLine: Standard formulas, cut-off values, and clinical interpretations for umbilical, cerebral, and venous Doppler
skill.annex.fetal_growth.doppler.why: Clinical decisions in fetal surveillance rely on precise mathematical indices and reference centiles. This annexure provides standard definitions, reference cut-offs, and clinical interpretations for umbilical, cerebral, and venous Doppler waveforms as well as amniotic fluid metrics.

probes.q: What threshold value of the cerebroplacental ratio indicates brain-sparing cerebral redistribution?
probes.a: A cerebroplacental ratio of less than 1.08 or below the 5th centile for gestational age indicates cerebral redistribution.

probes.q: What deepest vertical pocket measurement on ultrasound defines oligohydramnios?
probes.a: A single deepest vertical pocket of amniotic fluid measuring less than 2.0 centimetres defines oligohydramnios.

cases.title: A multigravida at 34 weeks with lagging fundal height and reduced fetal movements
cases.opening: Anita Sharma, a 26-year-old multigravida (gravida 2, para 1) at 34 weeks of gestation from a semi-urban district in Madhya Pradesh, has been referred by the community health centre because her fundal height measures only 29 cm and she noticed reduced fetal movements over the past two days. Introduce yourself and take a focused history.
cases.fallback: I am sorry, doctor, I did not understand that. Could you ask me in another way?

patient.occupation: Primary school teacher, currently on maternity leave
patient.residence: Semi-urban township near Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, living with husband and one child

skill.gen.appearance.finding: Thin, anxious young woman of light build, pale conjunctiva, no icterus, no peripheral oedema, calm but visibly distressed about the baby size.

skill.gen.vitals.finding: Blood pressure 138/88 mmHg right arm sitting, pulse 82 bpm regular, respiratory rate 18/min, afebrile, room air SpO2 98%.

skill.gen.edema.finding: No pedal, pretibial, or facial oedema detected on bilateral lower limbs.

skill.exam.obg.preg_prep_inspect.finding: Abdomen appears smaller than expected for 34 weeks gestation. Flanks are flat, no scars, linea nigra and striae gravidarum present.

skill.exam.obg.fundal_height.finding: Symphysis-fundal height measures 29 cm, lagging by 5 cm behind 34 completed weeks. Fundal palpation confirms small uterine volume.

skill.exam.obg.leopold.finding: Longitudinal lie, cephalic presentation, fetal parts felt very easily with sharp definition beneath maternal abdominal wall due to severe oligohydramnios. Head is non-engaged.

skill.exam.obg.fetal_heart.finding: Fetal heart sounds heard distinctly in right lower quadrant at 144 beats per minute, regular rhythm, no bradycardia on auscultation.

usg_biometry.label: Obstetric ultrasound biometry
usg_biometry.result: BPD 32 weeks, HC 32 weeks, FL 31 weeks, AC 28 weeks (AC < 3rd centile, marked head-sparing asymmetry with elevated HC/AC ratio). Estimated fetal weight 1480 g (< 3rd centile for 34 weeks). Anatomical survey reveals no gross structural anomalies.
usg_biometry.note: Confirms asymmetrical fetal growth restriction with abdominal circumference below the 3rd centile.

amniotic_fluid_index.label: Amniotic fluid volume assessment
amniotic_fluid_index.result: Single deepest vertical pocket (DVP) measures 1.4 cm (normal 2 to 8 cm). Four-quadrant Amniotic Fluid Index (AFI) is 3.8 cm (normal 5 to 25 cm).
amniotic_fluid_index.note: Severe oligohydramnios consistent with reduced fetal renal perfusion from compensatory circulatory redistribution.

umbilical_doppler.label: Umbilical artery and MCA Doppler
umbilical_doppler.result: Umbilical artery Doppler demonstrates absent end-diastolic flow (AEDF) on repeated cycles. Middle cerebral artery (MCA) Doppler shows pulsatility index below 5th centile indicating brain-sparing vasodilation. Cerebroplacental ratio (CPR) is 0.68 (abnormally low, < 1.08).
umbilical_doppler.note: Stage 2 placental insufficiency with umbilical artery absent end-diastolic flow and cerebral redistribution.

ctg_monitoring.label: Cardiotocography (CTG)
ctg_monitoring.result: Baseline fetal heart rate 142 bpm, moderate baseline variability of 8 to 12 bpm, two accelerations over 20 minutes, no late or variable decelerations observed.
ctg_monitoring.note: Normal reactive CTG trace with preserved short-term variability, ruling out acute fetal acidemia at present.

pre_eclampsia_labs.label: Maternal hypertensive workup and organ function
pre_eclampsia_labs.result: Haemoglobin 10.8 g/dL, platelet count 195,000/uL, serum creatinine 0.7 mg/dL, AST 28 U/L, ALT 24 U/L, urine dipstick trace protein (negative for significant proteinuria).
pre_eclampsia_labs.note: Gestational blood pressure elevation without laboratory evidence of pre-eclampsia or HELLP syndrome.

ductus_venosus_doppler.label: Ductus venosus Doppler velocimetry
ductus_venosus_doppler.result: Pulsatility index for veins (PIV) is 0.72 (within normal limits for 34 weeks). Forward positive a-wave maintained during atrial contraction.
ductus_venosus_doppler.note: Preserved forward ductus venosus a-wave confirms absence of advanced myocardial compromise or systemic acidemia.

differentialModel.answer: Pathological asymmetrical fetal growth restriction at 34 weeks with severe oligohydramnios and umbilical artery absent end-diastolic flow. Differentials include constitutionally small-for-gestational-age fetus, incorrect dates, congenital fetal infection, chromosomal abnormality, and ruptured membranes.

diagnosis.answer: Late-onset severe asymmetrical fetal growth restriction with oligohydramnios and umbilical artery absent end-diastolic flow at 34 weeks of gestation.

managementModel.answer: Admit to Level 3 obstetric centre with neonatal intensive care; administer antenatal corticosteroids for fetal lung maturation; monitor with daily CTG, ductus venosus Doppler and biophysical profile; plan delivery by caesarean section at 34 weeks due to absent end-diastolic flow; involve the neonatology team. Magnesium sulphate for neuroprotection is not indicated at this gestation under the pathway rule limiting it to planned delivery before 32 weeks.

teachingPoints: A symphysis-fundal height lagging by 3 cm or more behind gestational age is a red flag that mandates urgent ultrasound biometry, but biometry alone cannot differentiate a constitutionally small fetus from pathological growth restriction without Doppler velocimetry.

Asymmetrical growth restriction with abdominal circumference lagging behind head circumference reflects brain-sparing redistribution of fetal cardiac output to protect vital organs during chronic uteroplacental hypoxia.
Oligohydramnios in intact membranes is a hemodynamic sign of reduced fetal renal blood flow caused by hypoxaemia-induced circulatory redistribution, directly warning of chronic placental compromise.

Absent end-diastolic flow in the umbilical artery signifies that over 60 percent of the placental vascular tree is obliterated, transforming the delivery decision into an urgent balance between prematurity and fatal acidemia.

Antenatal corticosteroids must be administered ahead of anticipated preterm delivery prior to 34 to 36+6 weeks, and magnesium sulphate given for neuroprotection prior to 32 weeks, with delivery conducted in a facility equipped with Level 3 NICU care.
